conviction_note: The findings add up to about zero (-0.1). A Q3 fuel overrun, worked out from the EIA Gulf Coast series and the company's own $3.75/gal assumption and sensitivity, plus a Q4 outlook at $4.4+ jet fuel with no hedges, point down. Against that, the company said on 2026-09-29 that bookings and yields are robust, Delta absorbed a similar fuel miss for only -3%, and the stock has already fallen 17.6% in 20 sessions to a 52-week low with short interest rising. Scaled: abs_move 8.5 (between the 8.89 implied move and the 4.8 median, nudged up because the first quarterly outlook since the suspension is likely), p_up 47, a slight lean down because this name has fallen after 5 of its last 7 prints. The EPS number is likely below the bar (-40%); the stock reaction is near a coin flip, and the gap is because fuel is visible to everyone.
bar: The company's Q3 2026 guide: adjusted EPS $0.00-1.00 at $3.75/gal economic fuel, capacity +2-3%, RASM up low double digits, CASMex up low-to-mid single digits (8-K ex-99.1, 2026-07-21, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/766421/000076642126000036/ex9917212026earningsrelease.htm). Sell-side consensus is disputed. Earnings Whispers shows $0.35 EPS (whisper $0.34) and $4.31B revenue (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/ALK); earlier EW pages showed $0.48 and $0.37, and Benzinga's page shows $0.59 (probably stale). Because there are not two agreeing estimate sources, findings that depend on the consensus are capped small; print_vs_bar_pct is measured against EW's $0.35.
positioning_check: Short interest about 12.1M shares, 3.7 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (5.1 days at 09-15), up from about 10.7M in July (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/alk/short-interest/). Benzinga on 2026-10-09: 11.6% of float, 'Rising' (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ALK/sentiment). Elevated but below the 18-23% crowding that squeezed in earlier runs. The stock is 1.7% above its 52-week low and down 21.9% since the July print.

findings.finding: Q3 jet fuel ran well above the price Alaska guided on. The July guide assumed $3.75/gal economic fuel (July $3.60, August-September at the $3.85 spot curve). The EIA US Gulf Coast jet spot then averaged about $3.71 in August and about $4.38 in September, against roughly $3.2-3.3 in early July. That points to Q3 economic fuel of roughly $4.0-4.1. Alaska is unhedged (it exited its hedging program) and its CFO said at the investor day that '$0.10 is, for us, $120 million' a year. A $0.25-0.35/gal overrun is therefore about $75-105M pretax, or about $0.45-0.60 per share after the 35% tax rate on 113.5M shares. That puts the quarter near the bottom of the $0.00-1.00 guide and below EW's $0.35 consensus unless revenue makes up the gap.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ALK has fallen after 5 of its last 7 prints (median |move| 4.8%). July 2026 beat on EPS (-0.92 vs -0.98) and still fell 2.4%; April 2026, when guidance was suspended on fuel, fell 4.8%. Peer analog: Delta's Q3 fuel came in at $3.61 against a $3.15 July assumption, EPS was $1.72 against a $2.00-2.50 guide, and DAL fell only about 3% on 2026-10-09.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus has moved down (EW $0.48, then $0.37, then $0.35) but sits only $0.15 below the $0.50 guide midpoint, while the fuel arithmetic implies about $0.45-0.60 of overrun. Had it been fully priced, consensus would be near zero. Partly priced: the stock is down 17.6% in 20 sessions, and the fuel series is public to anyone.
findings.independence: The company's own documents give the assumption ($3.75/gal; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/766421/000076642126000036/alksupplemental2q26.htm) and the sensitivity, unhedged ($0.10 = $120M; https://news.alaskaair.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/AAG-Investor-Day-Transcript.pdf). Delta's Q3 shows the same overrun pattern against its July assumption (https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx). Retail Jet A rose in July, August and September (https://avweb.com/aviation-news/aviation-fuel-prices-september-2026/). The fuel-to-economic-price step is my inference, a proxy. The CFO also said on 09-29 that West Coast spot was barely above East Coast, which narrows Alaska's usual premium.

findings.finding: The Q4 outlook in tonight's release (management refused to guide Q4 at the 09-29 investor day) will be set at much higher fuel. Gulf Coast jet averaged about $4.35-4.6 in the October 5-16 sessions (EIA). Los Angeles jet hit $4.91/gal on 2026-10-09, its highest since April. Delta guided Q4 at about $4.25/gal all-in with a 7-9% operating margin and EPS of $1.15-1.65 below consensus. For an unhedged carrier with a seasonally weak Q4, that implies an outlook at or below breakeven. The investor day deck says Alaska is free-cash-flow positive only below $3.25/gal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: April 2026 guidance suspension on fuel: -4.8%. July 2026 Q3 guide well below consensus ($0.00-1.00 vs $1.22): stock fell only about 1.1% intraday (marketbeat) and 2.42% over the window. Delta's below-consensus Q4 guide on 10-09: about -3%.
findings.source_date: 2026-10-10 (KST; Bloomberg item on LA jet fuel $4.91)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The stock is down 8.6% in 5 sessions and 17.6% in 20, near the 52-week low, while jet fuel climbed through late September and October. A Q4 outlook not already in the price would have to be worse than Delta's template implies. If it were unpriced, the stock would not be at a 52-week low with calls slightly richer than puts.
findings.independence: EIA daily series (https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/EER_EPJK_PF4_RGC_DPGD.htm) and Delta's Q4 guide (https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx). The investor day 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/766421/000076642126000043/a2026investordaypresenta.htm) gives the FCF threshold. Shares the EIA series with finding 1, but this one is about a different period (Q4).

findings.finding: Revenue offset: at the 2026-09-29 investor day the CCO said 'the demand environment continues to be very robust', with 'very, very solid yields' in 21-day advance bookings, traction in Hawaii 21-plus days out, and 'very significant double-digit unit revenue increases' on some Honolulu long-haul. That supports the RASM side of the guide (low double digits) and fuel recapture. Delta's Q3 revenue rose 21% and its Q4 revenue guide is about +20%, with the CEO calling the consumer response 'quite strong'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue +10% and RASM +8.6% with premium +15%, but the fuel-driven loss dominated and the stock fell 2.42%. The revenue line has not paid on its own this year.
findings.why_not_priced: The comment was buried in the Q&A of a long-range investor day whose headlines were 2030 targets. The stock kept falling afterwards, as fuel rose. If it had been priced, consensus revenue would sit above the $4.31B that the guide arithmetic gives (Q3 2025 about $3.77B times about 1.14).
findings.independence: Delta's Q3 and Q4 revenue (https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx). The transcript is the same document as the hedging and sensitivity quote in finding 1, but a different statement.

Its fuel overrun and recapture commentary will move the airline group inside the same window, in either direction.

findings.finding: Capex lever: at the investor day the CFO said that if fuel pressure became acute, 'we would sit down and talk about the CapEx profile of the company. That's the quickest and easiest way to change the cash flow trajectory' (Boeing delivery stream; capex averaging $1.75B through 2030). At $4+ jet fuel against an FCF-positive threshold of $3.25, a capex cut or deferral announced with Q3 is a possible positive surprise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior capex-cut announcement at an ALK print found.
findings.why_not_priced: It is conditional and no plan was stated, only an option. The market has not been told a cut is coming; if it expected one, the FCF worry behind the drawdown would be smaller.

baseline_tension: The fuel negatives agree with the -17.6% 20-day run-up and the near-52-week-low price, so they are largely in the price. The skew (-1.83, calls slightly rich) and rising short interest cut slightly against a further down move. That pulls p_up toward 50, held at 47 only because this name has fallen after 5 of its last 7 prints.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside the guide): the Q3 fuel overrun lands at the low end of the company's $0.00-1.00 guide, i.e. inside what the market was told to expect, and the sell-side bar is disputed (EW $0.35 vs Benzinga $0.59). Finding 1 cut from -1.5 to -1.0.

Lessons 3 and 7 (own caveat, positioning): the Q4 fuel finding's own why_not_priced says it is mostly in a -17.6% run-up at a 52-week low, which agrees with the price. Finding 2 cut from -1.5 to -1.0.
Lesson 7: short interest of about 11.6% of float is rising but not crowded (below 18%) and the skew is mild, so the positioning finding was trimmed from +0.8 to +0.6 rather than enlarged.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): Delta absorbed the same fuel miss for -3%. Applied once, through p_up 45 to 47, not shrunk again in the findings.
Revenue offset (finding 3), UAL same-evening (finding 4) and the capex lever (finding 6) were left unchanged.
